takeaway: Meconium ileus: most patients have cystic fibrosis; impacted meconium in the ileum causes a mass and dilated small bowel loops.

question.text: A 3-day-old girl with cystic fibrosis has a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant. A plain abdominal X-ray shows dilated small bowel loops. What is the diagnosis?
question.say: A three-day-old girl with cystic fibrosis has a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant. A plain abdominal X-ray reveals dilated small bowel loops. What is the diagnosis?

lines.say: This is a three-day-old girl with cystic fibrosis. Most patients with meconium ileus have cystic fibrosis.

lines.text: The doctor feels a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant.
lines.say: The doctor feels a palpable mass in the right lower quadrant.

lines.text: The mass is meconium, the foetal stool, impacted in the ileum.
lines.say: (sigh) That mass is meconium, the foetal stool, impacted in the ileum.

lines.text: Behind the blockage the small bowel loops dilate.
lines.say: The obstructing meconium makes the small bowel loops dilate, more proximally, as the X-ray shows.

lines.text: Remember: cystic fibrosis, a right lower quadrant mass and dilated small bowel mean meconium ileus.
lines.say: Remember: cystic fibrosis, a mass in the right lower quadrant and dilated small bowel mean meconium ileus.
